note: The voters, the other models defined and the adjudicator, pinned. The adjudicator is `opus`, Claude Opus 5.5 run as confined Claude Code processes through files (`transport: handoff`); `claude`, Sonnet 5.5 through OpenRouter, stays defined, its pilot runs being on record, and `judge --adjudicator claude` picks it for one merge. After the pilot gemma replaced mistral as the third voter (mistral stays defined, its runs being on record). On 2026-10-08 hy3 (Tencent Hy3) replaced gemma: Gemma 4 31B returned HTTP 429 at every endpoint (`limit_source: upstream_provider_shared_pool`, a pool of the provider's that other keys share) and stalled the silver run at part 06; gemma stays defined, its runs being on record. `voters` and `adjudicator` name entries of `models`, so swapping a voter is one line there. `provider` is the tag the OpenRouter endpoint listing gives the endpoint (models/<id>/endpoints), and the runner checks the listing at run time: the endpoint must exist, have the quantisation pinned here, and support every parameter sent. `temperature` and `reasoning` are sent only when not null, since the request requires every parameter it sends: Mistral's endpoint lists no `reasoning`, and the Anthropic route lists no `temperature`. `reasoning` is passed through as OpenRouter's object; the adjudicator thinks at low effort, and `max_tokens` (16000) includes the thinking. `provider_fallback` lists every other endpoint of the same model that may run, in order after the pin by the listing's uptime of the day: at a quantisation in `quantizations`, supporting every parameter sent, not Fireworks, and not known bad; a model without `quantizations` (mistral) has alternatives at the same quantisation or a more precise one than `provider`'s listing gives, and `quantizations` is the one statement of what a voter may run at, for the pin and every alternative alike. When an endpoint fails in a way that is its own (HTTP 429 or 5xx through every wait, replies cut off on both halves of a split, a provider refusal) the runner abandons that run and starts a new one at the next endpoint, which asks every batch afresh; a run never changes endpoint. A network error here (connection refused, DNS, a timeout with no answer) is no endpoint's fault: the run stops and a rerun continues it. `--endpoint TAG` starts a run at a listed endpoint by hand. `settings.rate_limit_attempts` (4) is how many times a call that gets HTTP 429 is asked at one endpoint, where `http_attempts` (8) is the count for any other failure: a 429 whose `Retry-After` is longer than `longest_wait_s`, or the fourth, is the endpoint's own failure at once. `settings.failure_budget` (40) is the most calls that may fail in one step, across every wait, halving and switch; `settings.abstain_limit` (0.25) is the share of a voter run's sentences that may abstain before the run ends failed. deepseek's list leaves out DeepInfra's endpoint, which runs every reply to `max_tokens`. qwen's `quantizations` are fp8 and bf16: no other endpoint of its model lists bf16, so DeepInfra's bf16 is first and the fp8 endpoints follow, and a part that falls back is labelled at fp8, recorded per run. Endpoints left out of every list: Fireworks, a quantisation outside the voter's `quantizations` (fp4, fp16, `unknown`), and one that OpenRouter's list of zero-data-retention endpoints (endpoints/zdr) does not hold and that no run or screening has answered through with `data_collection: deny` (alibaba/fp8 and baidu/fp8 for deepseek, chutes/fp8 for qwen), since the listing says nothing of a provider's policy and OpenRouter refuses an endpoint that the request's `data_collection: deny` rules out. Pins and fallbacks from the listings of 2026-10-08. Every model has `license` (an SPDX id for an open-weight model), `license_url` (its model card, or for Claude the terms) and `license_checked`, the date its licence was last read, without which no run of it starts: a run copies the licence and the date into its `run.json` and `runs.tsv`, with the sha256 of this file. `external` holds the same for spaCy, which `register` records. The voters' cards (deepseek, qwen, gemma, hy3) and spaCy's (the model card and spaCy's LICENSE) were read again, and give that licence, on 2026-10-08.

spacy.license_note: MIT by its maker, Explosion; trained on OntoNotes 5 among other data

mistral.license_note: the card is matched to OpenRouter's `mistralai/mistral-large-2512` by name and date (Mistral Large 3, 2512), since OpenRouter's id names no card

opus.transport_note: not called by the runner: it writes a request file per call, and `label.py handoff-run` answers each with a `claude -p --safe-mode` process confined to an empty working directory (README.md, `handoff-run`). No price, temperature, reasoning or max_tokens is set: the harness decides them, and provenance (handoff/<run>/agent.json, in runs.tsv's settings) says so.
opus.license_note: run through Claude Code with the login of the person who runs it; when that login is a personal subscription, Anthropic's Consumer Terms (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms) govern it rather than the Commercial Terms

claude.temperature_note: not sent: with thinking on the API requires its default of 1, and the Anthropic route lists no temperature
